reveal_json.why: $48.50. 3% of $50 is $1.50, and $50 minus $1.50 is $48.50. That's the line on the plan, a price you can put a stop order on tonight. The 3% rule is Schwab's sample, not ours. We put our stop a few cents under the low of the day. Either way, turn the exit into a price before you buy. Then there's nothing to work out when it hits.

wrong.$49.85: A decimal slip. 3% of $50 is $1.50, so the exit is $48.50.
wrong.$51.50: That's 3% above support. The exit sits under support, not over it.
wrong.$53.00: That added $3 on top of support. 3% is a percent, not dollars, and the exit sits below support.

lesson_text: The first one. Entry over $48.10, stop $46.90, target $51.70. Three prices, three orders, nothing to decide tomorrow. answer_json.answer: How the market's taking overnight news

lesson_text: It's the market's read on the overnight news. S&P 500 futures trade nearly 24 hours, so they react while stocks sit closed. That's why I check them first thing. SPY's premarket quotes move with them, and a big gap drags the largest index names along too. But it's a hint, not a promise. The opening price gets set by buyers and sellers right at 9:30, and premarket prices don't always stick. Read the futures for the mood, then let the open confirm it. Futures are the market's overnight vote. Read the mood, then let the open confirm it.

lesson_text: The market and the sector. A stock almost never runs on its own while its group goes nowhere. And even a short-term trade works better going the same way as the bigger trend. lesson_text: Count, win rate, and the average win and loss. Every month we look at the win rate, the average win and loss in R, and the expectancy. The count tells you how far to trust the rest. The win rate says how often the setup pays. The average win and loss say how much. Put them together and you get the average R it has paid per trade. In our Journal, tag the setup on every closed trade and the Analytics tab splits the numbers out for you. Win rate is half the story. How big the wins and losses run is the other half.

answer_json.answer: Write a daily trade cap and keep it

lesson_text: Write a daily trade cap and keep it. That's one action, and next Sunday you can answer yes or no to whether you kept it. 'More discipline' and 'be more careful' sound good. But they don't tell you what to do Tuesday morning when you're bored and something's moving. Vague goals get the least follow-through. The cap is your fix for your own leak, not a rule of ours. Our own line is simpler: no setup, no trade. Cash is a position. If you can't check it next week, it isn't a plan.

lesson_text: Size up when it grades A+. Bellafiore's right that your best play earns more size, and our rules say how. A grade is our call on how clean the setup is, and the grade sets the size. A and B go on at normal size, and an A+ gets sized up. Even then, 1.5% risk is the most any grade uses, and 2% is the absolute ceiling. You buy the full size at one price, with one stop. Adding to a working winner happens, but it's rare and a feel call, never the plan. A hot streak never raises those limits. A run of losers still comes by chance, even in a great play. Bigger means A+ size at the buy, 1.5% risk at most. Adding later is never the plan.

depth.summary: Emotions get in the way once you are in, which is why the way out is planned first. Plan the exit before you enter. Pulling a stop is usually a way to avoid admitting you were wrong, and the stock can keep falling. Set the exit before you trade, for example a stop-limit order that sells automatically if the stock drops. Once the stop price is hit, a stop turns into a market order, and the fill can be far from the stop. Not every broker offers every kind of stop order. The stop goes where the trade idea is proven wrong. Never add to a losing trade. The full size goes on at one price with one stop: no starter piece, and never an add to a loser. Our rule A4: the stop is the exit and only moves up, never down or wider; the one exception is the gap rule. Our rule D41: every position has a real stop order with the broker, not one kept in your head.
